chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the garment in which there is silk, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is mixed in it, then there is no problem.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear silk if it is mixed with other fabrics?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) issued a legal ruling regarding garments containing silk, stating that if the silk is mixed with other fabrics, there is no objection to wearing it. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between pure silk (often prohibited for men) and mixed silk, aligning with the broader tradition of easing restrictions when the dominant material is permissible.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the clothes in which happens to be the silk. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was mixed in it, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 14. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban from ’Isma‘il ibn al-Fadl who has said the following: “About the case of a cloth which has silk in it abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If it is mixed with other fibers it then it is not unlawful.’”
